text: A capsule preserves an exact current input.
A next operation can be specific independently of scheduling.
The original source for a next operation can remain unchanged while its parent record changes.
The next operation has prerequisites.
A future observation can arrive too late to alter a choice.
Information has a price and a contingent-use policy.
A price can make perfect information unattractive despite action sensitivity.
Noisy information needs an observation model to price its value.
The goal may change before the saved operation resumes.
A preserved queue can contain completed and pending entries.
The actual current model can perform a ready next operation now.
A timing method’s value must include what it causes to happen and what it costs.
Input can be exact, truncated, paraphrased or absent.
A capsule is a stored payload; siblings include a bookmark, a command specification and a full checkpoint.
The restoration operation uses the saved string rather than reconstructing it from memory.
Preparation time and restoration time are separate events.
Specific-unscheduled, vague-scheduled, specific-scheduled and neither are distinct states.
Payload specificity and initiation status are separate axes.
A current executor can use a ready payload; a future executor still needs initiation.
An observed scheduled state has an actual service acknowledgment.
A source hash can refer to the origin map, the next skill or an input dataset.
Origin changed/skill unchanged is observed in capsule-current-check.json.
Byte identity and role in the action’s validity are different axes.
A completion-status edit can follow the original frozen-input capture.
Prerequisites include evidence, capability, permission and a still-valid goal.
One prerequisite may fail while other independent operations remain ready.
The chosen dependency graph reflects actual data/control requirements.
A blocked local branch need not imply a blocked whole portfolio.
Arrival can precede, equal or follow an opportunity deadline.
The opportunity can persist, degrade or disappear.
Information accuracy and arrival time are separate dimensions.
The action remains feasible at the time the policy uses the observation.
In AEX34 c=1; c=0 and c=4 are alternative declared prices.
After observing failure the policy may decline or be forced to act.
Observation precision and ability to condition action are separate.
Information purchase is an option among immediate action, abstention and partial investigation.
For the declared payoff model, wait−act=3−4p.
At p=.4 wait gains; at .75 ties; at .9 loses under expected payoff.
Payoffs, price, probability and available actions match the declared model.
An expected-payoff chooser and a worst-state chooser can use different criteria on the same input.
Noise can be symmetric, asymmetric, state-dependent or unspecified.
Sensitivity and specificity may vary independently.
An “80% accurate” label can conceal a base rate and asymmetric errors.
Conditional observation probabilities are available for the expected-value calculation.
A later user instruction can alter a previously appropriate next step.
The old result remains historical even if the current recommendation is invalidated.
The later user can value a different target from the present model’s pending queue.
The resumed operation reads the current governing instruction.
An entry can be pending, performed, blocked or superseded.
History retention and next-choice eligibility are separate properties.
This is a state-transition system; siblings include build queues and study protocols.
Selecting one ready item differs from asserting the whole program will complete autonomously.
Tool execution, written proposal and human assignment have different observed statuses.
A host returns an operation result; a human may inspect it later without being its executing actor.
The required tools and source are currently available for that operation.
Current tool completion is not a receipt for a future session.
Elapsed delay, paid resource and foregone opportunity are distinct cost candidates.
A representation can improve restoration while leaving execution unobserved.
An actual comparison does not credit a hypothetical future act as performed.
Timing evaluation is both a control question and a decision-value question.
